text:
sourav: quick share - i ran a small experiment to cut down kv cache fragmentation and memory growth from long chat sessions. idea: tag prefix entries with a lightweight TTL cohort and a prefix-length bucket, plus optional short sticky session pinning for N requests. results below.

kevin: can you TL;DR the change? what exactly is in the cache key now?

sourav: tl;dr: cache key changed from `model:session_id:prefix_hash` -> `model:cohort:len_bucket:prefix_hash`. cohort is derived from a cheap rolling hash of user/session+recent activity and a hotness score; len_bucket is one of [1-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024] tokens. we attach a 5–30m TTL per entry based on cohort activity. optional session-sticky pin keeps the last K prefixes pinned for the originating session for up to 5 requests to avoid immediate thrash on conversational turn-backs.

maya: profiling numbers? i care about memory growth per-hour and hit-rate change.

kevin: pasted sampling run from a 12h replay, 32-GPU worker, mixed Llama2-13B models.

kevin: ```
# baseline (no cohort keys)
avg_kv_entries_per_gpu: 1.1M
mem_growth_rate: 1.2GB/hour
overall_kv_hit_rate: 21.8%
p99_generation_latency: 142ms

# cohort+len_bucket+ttl
avg_kv_entries_per_gpu: 430k
mem_growth_rate: 0.25GB/hour
overall_kv_hit_rate: 48.6%
p99_generation_latency: 145ms  # +3ms observed
``` 

iris: those look promising. where did the saved entries go? were they cold small prefixes or long tail unique keys?

sourav: mostly long-tail unique prefixes from noisy system prompts & user ids that used to create unique session-level keys. cohorting aggregated many of those into the same hot buckets so reuse increased. len_bucketing prevented tiny prefixes from polluting large-key maps and reduced fragmentation of the slab allocator.

devon: any regressions? warmup time? do we see more false positives (wrong prefix used) leading to hallucinations or truncation issues?

sourav: functional correctness unchanged — we still store full KV arrays keyed by prefix_hash; cohort/len_bucket only affect which bucket/TTL the entry lives in and which prefix keys we prefetch/coalesce. we do add a cheap verification check when serving: if prefix length > stored_len + 8 then skip reuse (edge safety). no evidence of hallucination regressions in the 12h run. unit tests + golden prompts unchanged.

maya: cost win looks huge. what about p99 increase? microbench might explain +3ms.

kevin: p99 bump traced to extra hash ops and a tiny atomic metadata update during cache insertion. measured add: ~2.5ms on 4096 token contexts for first token in prefix reuse path. can be mitigated by moving some metadata updates to background async writes and batching the hash ops into the request prep stage.

sourav: my proposal: ship as canary to 10% of traffic on Dedicated and Hosted for 48h. add per-cohort metrics: hit_rate, evictions_per_min, avg_ttl, mem_bytes. pinning default off for hosted but on for Dedicated (configurable).

iris: add a /metrics tag: `kv_prefetch.cohort.<cohort_id>.hit_rate` and `kv_prefetch.len_bucket.<bucket>.entries` + alert if cohort_evictions > 500/min.

deploy-bot: canary deployment started by @sourav at 2026-03-18T15:02:31Z (canary=10%).

devon: nits: please add a smoke test that replays a synthetic long-chat scenario to catch any unexpected mem growth within 2h.

sourav: yep added a test in `eng-runtime/test/kv_cohort_replay.py` that replays 2000 conversations with back-and-forth and asserts mem_growth < 0.4GB/hour and hit_rate >= 40%.

kevin: long-term followups: (1) adaptive ttl per-cohort using actual reuse half-life, (2) cross-worker cohort sharing metadata to preemptively prefetch hot prefixes, (3) consider GPU-local compacted slabs for len_bucket>1024 to avoid fragmentation under long sequences.

maya: sounds good. i'm +1 for canary. please post canary results thread with the new metrics after 48h.

sourav: will do. posting the initial dashboard link: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/kv/cohort-prefetch?org=eng (contains per-cohort heatmap and mem-growth timeseries).
